security_audit.summary: Most alerts are benign JavaScript syntax, image data, Chinese documentation, and negative test fixtures. Confirmed risks include unpinned automatic updates, inherited secrets, and unsafe preview input handling. Release-note trust and selector interpolation add injection risks; no evidence of intentional malware was found.

remediation.issue: Skill loading can execute an unpinned GitHub updater and replace audited files.
remediation.suggestion: Make updates opt-in, require confirmation, pin the CLI to a reviewed commit, and verify replacement artifacts before loading them.

remediation.issue: The downloaded updater inherits all environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Pass a minimal environment allowlist and only explicitly authorized authentication values. Exclude unrelated project and service credentials.

remediation.issue: The local preview server uses string-prefix containment and follows symlinks.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve the root and target with realpath, enforce path-relative containment, and test encoded traversal, sibling prefixes, and escaping symlinks.

remediation.issue: Unchecked screenshot state names can escape the output directory.
remediation.suggestion: Generate safe artifact identifiers independently from state text, enforce output containment, and reject escaping paths before writing.

remediation.issue: Contact-sheet state labels are inserted into executable HTML.
remediation.suggestion: Render captions with textContent or HTML escaping. Apply a contact-sheet CSP that disables scripts and external resources.

remediation.issue: Remote release notes are presented to agents without a clear trust boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Treat release notes as quoted untrusted data, remove control characters, and never execute or adopt instructions from updater output.

remediation.issue: The type action embeds a raw selector in evaluated JavaScript.
remediation.suggestion: Serialize every dynamic string with JSON.stringify, including error messages. Add regression tests with quotes and code-like selectors.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Release Notes Enter Agent Instructions
semantic_findings.description: Remote release notes are copied into updater notices after minimal trimming. SKILL.md tells agents to relay these notices, creating a prompt-injection channel.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The remote notes flow directly into output the agent consumes. No embedded attack was found, but the source-to-instruction trust boundary is explicit.

semantic_findings.title: Selector Interpolation Allows Browser Code Injection
semantic_findings.description: The type action inserts its selector directly into a quoted JavaScript error message. Crafted quotes can execute unintended code in the inspected page.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The querySelector argument is serialized, but the same selector is interpolated without escaping in the error string. An isolated expression check confirmed injection.

high_findings.title: Python subprocess.run
high_findings.description: result = subprocess.run([npx, "-y", CLI, "update", name, "--path", str(ROOT), "--json"], env=env,
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The updater runs npx -y against an unpinned GitHub CLI and replaces the installed skill without fresh consent. Compromised upstream code could execute locally.

high_findings.title: Python environment access
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The updater copies every environment variable into the unpinned downloaded CLI process. This exposes unrelated credentials to code outside the audited package.

high_findings.title: Synchronous file operations
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The server reads files after a string-prefix containment check, which accepts sibling directories and follows escaping symlinks. Local requests can disclose files outside the preview root.

content.value_statement: Generic interface drafts often lack clear visual priorities and meaningful alternatives. Oil UI guides design exploration, prototype comparison, and refinement using actual screen evidence.
actual_capabilities: Guide distinct design directions through product categories, layout, typography, color, imagery, and motion.
Build portable comparison pages from local HTML, PNG, JPEG, WebP, and loopback development URLs.
Compare desktop and mobile previews, show a baseline, filter candidates, and copy selections with notes.
Guide screenshot recreation and interface refinement while preserving project design conventions.
Capture screenshots, state sheets, text-masked views, and motion evidence with the bundled browser tool.
Structure one-round visual reviews using current screenshots, task constraints, and concrete improvement suggestions.
limitations: Business logic, data flow, implementation architecture, and comprehensive testing are outside the design scope.
Comparison generation requires Python 3.10+; capture requires Node.js 22+ and a compatible browser; MP4 assembly requires ffmpeg.
Live previews require running local servers; visual validation and independent review depend on host capabilities.
The audit found updater and preview-input risks; disable automatic updates and avoid untrusted inputs until remediation.

use_cases.title: Compare Product Directions
use_cases.description: Explore distinct booking-product interfaces, compare representative previews, and record a selected direction before implementation.

use_cases.title: Refine Existing Interfaces
use_cases.description: Improve hierarchy, spacing, typography, and motion while preserving existing brand assets and shared design conventions.

use_cases.title: Review Design Evidence
use_cases.description: Assess current screens against audience needs and project constraints, then receive prioritized visual recommendations without changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this homepage screenshot for visual hierarchy and readability. Give three prioritized recommendations. Do not modify files or run update scripts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: request a read-only visual review.

prompt_templates.title: Explore Three Directions
prompt_templates.prompt: Explore three visual directions for our course-booking product. Compare layout, typography, color, and imagery. Ask me to select one before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Local Prototypes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my local candidates to build a comparison page with a baseline and desktop and mobile views. Disable updates and review inputs first.

prompt_templates.title: Refine and Verify a Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Refine this checkout flow within our design system. Capture desktop, mobile, and motion evidence. Review once, document gaps, and leave business logic unchanged.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: improve an existing interface using actual evidence.

output_examples.input: Compare three design directions for an exhibition page.
output: Direction A prioritizes artwork, quiet navigation, and restrained typography.
Direction B uses editorial headlines and contrasting image scales.
Direction C uses a structured catalog layout with compact navigation.
The comparison presents the same exhibition content and records the selected direction.

output_examples.input: Review a mobile checkout screenshot without changing files.
output: Priority 1: separate the order total from secondary delivery details.
Priority 2: increase spacing between the address summary and payment controls.
Priority 3: preserve the primary action when long labels wrap.
A static screenshot cannot verify submission behavior or motion.

best_practices: Provide real content, brand constraints, target devices, and a clear delivery scope before exploring directions.
Disable automatic updates during controlled work and review candidate files, commands, state names, and selectors before execution.
Evaluate actual screens at readable sizes and record unverified interactions, missing assets, and review limitations.
anti_patterns: Treating cosmetic color changes as distinct design directions.
Claiming visual or interaction validation from source inspection or a single static screenshot.
Running unreviewed updates or third-party preview inputs with project credentials available.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The text workflow supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Available browser, image, and isolated-review capabilities depend on the host.

faq.question: What dependencies do the optional tools need?
faq.answer: Comparison generation needs Python 3.10+. Capture needs Node.js 22+ and Chrome, Chromium, or Edge. MP4 assembly also needs ffmpeg.

faq.question: Can comparison pages work offline?
faq.answer: Embedded HTML and image candidates can work offline. Live URL candidates require their local development servers.

faq.question: Does this replace engineering tests?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on design judgment and visible evidence, not business logic, architecture, comprehensive tests, or production deployment.

faq.question: What should I know about automatic updates?
faq.answer: Loading can trigger unpinned updater execution. Set OIL_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 for reminders only, or OIL_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 to disable checks. Review updates separately.

faq.question: Does the skill promote a paid version?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a one-time Oil UI Pro recommendation and context-specific purchase suggestions. Paid features are not included in this package.
